grants.description: Verify your identity using your GOV.UK One Login credentials
grants.purpose: To confirm you are who you say you are and that you are the named executor or closest relative

grants.description: Access your estate valuation and Inheritance Tax determination from HMRC
grants.purpose: To verify the estate valuation and Inheritance Tax position reported in your probate application

grants.description: Share the death certificate with HMCTS Probate Service
grants.purpose: To verify the death and establish the legal basis for probate application

grants.description: Upload and share the original will with HMCTS Probate Registry
grants.purpose: The will becomes part of the public record and determines who can apply for probate and how the estate is distributed

grants.description: Share contact details for all executors named in the will or other applicants
grants.purpose: To contact all executors for legal declaration signing and to ensure agreement on who applies

grants.description: Provide detailed information about the deceased's assets, property, and debts
grants.purpose: To enable the Probate Service to review and grant probate based on accurate estate information

grants.description: Provide information about beneficiaries named in the will or entitled under intestacy rules
grants.purpose: To ensure the correct distribution of the estate according to the will or intestacy rules

revocation.mechanism: Contact HMCTS Probate Service at contactprobate@justice.gov.uk or revoke through your GOV.UK account
revocation.effect: Application will be cancelled if consent is revoked before grant issued. If grant already issued, revocation will not affect the grant but will prevent further data sharing.

delegation.limitations: Agent CANNOT: sign the legal declaration on your behalf (you or all executors must sign personally); make payment for probate fees; upload the original will (you must provide); resolve executor disputes; make legal decisions about contested applications; act as your legal representative in court; determine beneficiaries or change the will; authorize changes to estate valuation.
